title: How every Claude call in the app shares one wrapper
purpose: Show the convention every AI call in the app follows: each script has a tiny ~10-line wrapper that loads its system prompt from a sibling .md file and calls one shared function (call_claude). Once the teacher understands this diagram, every Claude call in Surf makes sense — there is exactly one place we hit the API. This diagram is GLOBAL: it gets updated each phase as new Claude callers are added.
audience: non-engineer teammates and the grading teacher

groups.label: The shared wrapper (one place; every call goes through it)
Phase 1 callers (3 scripts, all follow the same 10-line pattern)

nodes.label: .env (gitignored)
nodes.description: Holds ANTHROPIC_API_KEY locally. Loaded automatically by python-dotenv on import

nodes.label: claude_client.call_claude
nodes.description: The single entry point. Inputs: system_prompt (string), user_message (string), expect_json (bool). Default model: claude-sonnet-4-6. Default max_tokens: 8192

nodes.label: Prompt caching (cache_system=True)
nodes.description: Wraps the system prompt in a cache_control block — same system prompt called within 5 min only pays ~10% of full input cost. Massive savings for batched MCQ calls

nodes.label: JSON code-fence stripping
nodes.description: Tolerant to ```json / ```JSON / leading-space variants Claude occasionally emits. Returns a parsed dict when expect_json=True

nodes.label: factsheet_cleaner.clean_factsheet
nodes.description: Called once per uploaded factsheet PDF

nodes.label: mcq_generator.generate_mcqs
nodes.description: Called once per batch of ≤10 slides — multiple times per lecture
